raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**Update (Oct 27): rebased onto current main (incl. #61875's MoE dispatch), and a fail-closed exactness contract was added in response to review feedback below.** The conversion now *rejects* input it cannot encode exactly instead of assuming exactness: invalid e8m0 scales (0xFF) fail the load, and per-value representability is verified against a per-e2m1-code exponent-spread bound (the byte-110 underflow and byte-255 cases from @AranKomat's review now raise, before any layer parameter is replaced). The exactness claim is therefore **exact for inputs accepted by the load-time check**, not unconditional. Verification counters are aggregated on device with a single host sync per converted tensor, keeping the load-time cost off the hot path.

## Purpose / positioning after #61875

Since this PR was opened, #61875 landed a native SM90 route for the same checkpoints: `Mxfp4MoEMethod(activation_key=kMxfp8Dynamic)` + Humming W4A8 kernels (4-bit storage kept, decode-heavy focused). On stacks with humming-kernels ≥0.1.18 that path is the strictly better choice (no 2× expert memory).

This PR covers the remaining gap: **weight-dequant → block-FP8 runs on the existing block-FP8 MoE kernel**, no humming-kernels dependency, and targets prefill/TTFT rather than decode — measured single-request TTFT prefill throughput 1.38–1.53× over Marlin W4A16 at 2k–8k input (H20, TP=4, numbers below unchanged). It is opt-in (`VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1`, default off, Marlin untouched) and fail-closed at load. If maintainers prefer to consolidate on the W4A8 direction and drop this, no objection — happy to pivot. The platform-independent fail-closed conversion contract and its tests may still be independently useful.

## Measured evidence (unchanged from original post)

- End-to-end prefill (single request, TTFT, unique prompts, TP=4, H20):
  | input len | Marlin W4A16 (default) | dequant→FP8 | speedup |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2048 | 7020 tok/s | 10752 tok/s | 1.53× |
  | 4096 | 8129 tok/s | 11882 tok/s | 1.46× |
  | 8192 | 8396 tok/s | 11623 tok/s | 1.38× |
- GSM8K (full 1319, 8-shot, greedy, H20, TP=4): Marlin 94.47% vs dequant→FP8 w8a8 93.93% (Δ −0.54pp, within run-to-run noise at this n). Re-encoded expert *weights* are exact for inputs accepted by the load-time check; the only added quantization is w8a8 activations.

## Changes

- `vllm/envs.py`: `VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT` (default off).
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/fp4_dequant.py`: `cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block` (fails closed on inexact input) + `DsV4Fp4DequantMoEMethod(Fp8MoEMethod)` (MXFP4 create_weights → validated re-encode → FP8 kernel).
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/quant_config.py`: opt-in routing ahead of the `Mxfp4MoEMethod(activation_key=kMxfp8Dynamic)` dispatch.
- `tests/quantization/test_dsv4_fp4_dequant.py`: exactness over sampled shapes/spreads, byte-110 underflow, byte-255 non-finite scale, per-value spread boundary (14/15/17), extreme-spread rejection, and no-partial-parameter-replacement on failure. (New rejection tests to be exercised on the next CI/H20 run.)

## Note

AI assistance was used to prepare this change; the submitter has reviewed every line and is responsible for the change and its tests/evals.

🚀

Additional throughput A/B on Hopper for this opt-in path (H20, TP=4, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--max-model-len 524288`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, 32 concurrent requests, 0% prefix-cache hit). Throughput read from the engine's Prometheus counters (`vllm:generation_tokens_total` / `vllm:prompt_tokens_total`), reported as total tokens / wall time.

### Decode (1-token input, forced N-token output via `ignore_eos`, 32 concurrent)

| output len | default (Marlin W4A16) | this PR (dequant->FP8) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2k  | 1,642 tok/s | 1,856 tok/s | 1.13x |
| 10k | 1,637 tok/s | 1,841 tok/s | 1.12x |

Per-request ~51 -> ~58 tok/s. Both engines are fully batched (`Running: 32`), and decode rate is independent of output length. So the FP8-tensor-core expert path also helps decode (~1.13x), not just prefill.

### Prefill (unique random prompts, `max_tokens=1`, 32 concurrent)

| input len | default (Marlin W4A16) | this PR (dequant->FP8) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8k  | 6,545 tok/s | 13,335 tok/s | 2.04x |
| 64k | 8,242 tok/s | 11,370 tok/s | 1.38x |

The prefill speedup narrows as context grows (attention increasingly dominates over the MoE GEMM), but stays positive.

### Trade-off (unchanged)

FP8 experts use 2x the weight memory vs MXFP4, which lowers KV capacity: at this config per-GPU available KV cache is 83.9 GiB (Marlin) -> 53.7 GiB (this PR), i.e. GPU KV cache size 5.70M -> 3.65M tokens. Accuracy is unaffected (GSM8K 1319-item parity, 94.47% vs 93.93%, within noise), as noted in the PR body.

### How to use

Opt-in via the `VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1` env var (default off; without it the model runs the usual MXFP4/Marlin path). Example on Hopper:

```bash
VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 524288 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
```

To go back to the default (MXFP4/Marlin W4A16), just unset the variable. On startup the worker log shows the FP8 path is active: `Using TRITON Fp8 MoE backend` and the MoE running as `fp8_w8a8` block `[128, 128]`.
Gentle ping @yewentao256 — as a code owner for the quantization layers this touches, would you have a chance to take a look when you get time? Happy to address any feedback. Thanks!

We have complementary gfx942 / DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash work for this design and would prefer to coordinate it with this PR rather than open another generic MXFP4-to-FP8 loader.

Our local TP8 checkpoint experiment keeps the existing packed-W4 shard loading, then converts only routed experts before native block-FP8 kernel setup. The additional ROCm/V4.1 contracts we found are:

- **Gate/up padding:** the TP-local intermediate width is 288, which is not 128-aligned. Gate and up halves must be padded separately to 384; padding the concatenated tensor changes the gate/up split.
- **FP8 format handling:** FN-to-FNUZ normalization and scale compensation should stay in the existing ROCm FP8 method rather than being implemented as raw E4M3FN byte reinterpretation.
- **Checkpoint metadata:** dense UE8M0 interpretation and the checkpoint-wide `expert_dtype=fp4` remain unchanged. Only routed-expert compute state and the padded extent change.
- **Clamp semantics:** the positive clamp of 10 must survive the selected MoE dispatch. Our separate evidence on #53875 covers the existing fused SiLU/quant path; equality of stored weights alone is not sufficient to establish model-output equivalence.

On the historical local implementation, all 320 layer/rank expert conversions had zero relative RMSE against decoded W4 values. Independent TP8 arithmetic checks and changed-input graph replays passed before model loading. GSM8K-100 completed at 99%, which we treat only as an initial corruption screen, not paired quality qualification. Resident expert memory, including padding and scales, increased by 2.5104167x.

These results are **not tests of this PR's current head**, and we are not claiming a current-main incremental serving gain.

Would an opt-in ROCm/V4.1 extension with platform-native dtype handling and separate gate/up padding fit the intended scope of this PR, or would you prefer it as a follow-up after the base conversion lands? We will keep the code local and human-review it before any submission.

This coordination note was prepared with Codex assistance.

Follow-up from the AMD/TP8 review against `b575b5fc05d65a809c68cf3137ac925b3fb30294`.

### 1. Existing ROCm normalization should be reused

`Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` already performs FN-to-FNUZ normalization and scale compensation. I verified that tensor arithmetic against the re-encoded values on CPU, so an additional byte reinterpretation in this loader would be unnecessary.

### 2. The current MXFP4 conversion is not unconditionally lossless

This limitation is platform-independent.

A 128x128 matrix of packed `0x11` weights, with microscale byte 127 except for one group at byte 110, contains `2^-18` values that the current conversion rounds to zero. Microscale byte 255 also produces non-finite values without rejection.

These are synthetic contract counterexamples, not evidence that a released checkpoint contains either case. The existing exactness test samples scale bytes 119..127, so it does not exercise these boundaries.

I have a local fail-closed reconstruction check plus a 128-aligned allocation extension for 288-wide TP shards. The allocation change uses the packed loader's existing separate gate/up halves and unpadded rank offsets; it does not change global `expert_dtype` or dense UE8M0 scales.

Initial local status:
- 13 CPU source-contract cases pass.
- Both new rejection cases fail against the parent implementation as expected.
- These tests exercise extracted tensor/loader logic only. They do not establish native loading, ROCm execution, clamp correctness, or model quality.

### 3. Native gfx942 loader qualification

A later native pass reached 36 actual-import CPU/GPU tests across all eight TP offsets and the conversion/normalization cases.

That exposed an ordering constraint: `Fp8MoEMethod` chooses/refines its backend before the later dimension-rounding hook. A local width of 288 therefore selects an unsupported 32x32 block scheme unless the method's copied config is 128-aligned before backend selection.

Keeping checkpoint metadata unpadded while changing that internal ordering passes native allocation and FN/FNUZ post-load checks for eight synthetic experts. The observed extra allocation cost was roughly 1.8-2.4 s and 122-123 MiB peak HBM in this synthetic test, not a full-checkpoint measurement.

The loaded expert was not yet qualified at this point: M=1 failed the independent positive-clamp oracle, and the selected two-stage CK SiLU path exposes no stage-1 clamp argument. I did not treat this as evidence about split-K or other arithmetic, and no model startup or serving claim followed.

### 4. Native layer compute qualification

A subsequent guarded Triton fallback passed the native layer compute gate.

Two changes were required:

1. Preserve the requested FP8 backend while giving the temporary MXFP4 allocation helper its own `auto` backend.
2. Exclude clamp-active inputs from the existing unclamped SiLU/block128-FP8 shortcut, matching the guard already discussed in #53875.

With those changes, 40 actual-import CPU/GPU tests pass. Real packed allocation/post-loading and clamped M=1/8/16 forwards pass the unchanged independent FP32 oracle, along with three changed-route graph replays per size. Eager NRMSE was 0.059519 / 0.051727 / 0.055704. M=1 is close to the 0.06 bound, so this is still not a substitute for full checkpoint/model validation.

A four-arm diagnostic also separated two CK issues: the M=1 split-K defect and ignored positive clamp are distinct. Disabling split-K repairs only the unclamped case. We are not claiming a CK fix.

### Scope

All of the above is local candidate work with packaged vLLM / Torch / ROCm dependencies. It is **not** a test of this entire PR head or current main, and there is still no endpoint speedup claim.

The extension remains local pending human review, coordination on the base PR, full-checkpoint coverage, and paired model testing. I will not open a duplicate loader PR while this work is being coordinated here.

Analysis and testing used Codex assistance.

Thanks for the careful counterexamples and for keeping the ROCm work coordinated here. I confirmed both issues against `b575b5fc`.

The current unconditional **lossless** wording is too broad:

- With a block maximum scale byte of 127, byte 110 gives `s = 2^-17`. For an E2M1 value of 0.5, the value presented to E4M3FN is `0.5 * 64 * 2^-17 = 2^-12`, below E4M3FN's minimum positive subnormal (`2^-9`). It therefore rounds to zero even though the decoded source value is `2^-18`.
- Scale byte 255 propagates a non-finite value through `amax` and the block scale, and the current conversion does not reject it.

The existing exactness test samples scale bytes only in `119..127`, so it proves exactness for that sampled range, not for arbitrary MXFP4 scales. Likewise, the successful DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 load and model evaluations are useful corruption/non-inferiority checks, but they are not an exhaustive load-time reconstruction check. I therefore cannot claim from the current evidence that every tensor in the released checkpoint satisfies an unconditional exactness contract. Conversely, the synthetic cases do not show that the released checkpoint actually contains such values.

I agree this should fail closed before retaining any lossless claim. The fix I intend for this PR is to:

1. reject invalid/non-finite E8M0 scales before conversion;
2. verify that every normalized source value is exactly representable after the E4M3FN cast before replacing the layer parameters;
3. add targeted tests for the byte-110 underflow and byte-255 cases, plus the exactness boundary; and
4. narrow the wording to **lossless for inputs accepted by the load-time exactness check**.

The validation can be aggregated on device and checked once per converted tensor/layer so that it does not add a host synchronization per expert. Until a full checkpoint scan reports zero mismatches, I will keep the released-checkpoint claim limited to the serving/evaluation evidence already reported.

For scope, I would prefer to land the platform-independent correctness contract and fail-closed checks here first, then handle the ROCm/V4.1 extension as a coordinated follow-up. The separate gate/up padding, FN/FNUZ handling, backend-selection ordering, clamp behavior, and CK/Triton fallback are substantial platform-specific contracts and deserve their own review and validation rather than being folded into this correction. Please keep the local work; it sounds directly useful once this base is solid.

Thanks again — this identified a real gap in both the implementation contract and the test coverage.

We run **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (not V4) in production on a single node of 8×H20 (SM90) with stock MXFP4/Marlin, so we're a direct candidate for this opt-in path. Two things that may be useful:

**1. Current Marlin baseline on the same class of hardware** — unique-marker bench, 0 errors, zero CPU offload, util 0.92, fp8 KV:

| | value |
|---|---|
| conc64 / mt=256 | 2434 tok/s |
| conc256 / mt=256 | 4440 tok/s |
| conc256 short-output | ~3300 tok/s |
| 128K cold prefill TTFT | 17.3 s (~6900 tok/s equiv) |

**2. The "GPU busy but memory idle" shape also shows up on this family**: on V4-Flash (H20, TP=4) we measured `utilization.memory` at 14% while `utilization.gpu` hit 100%. Consistent with the MoE path being latency/launch-bound rather than MMA- or bandwidth-bound — i.e. the motivation for moving the routed-expert GEMMs onto FP8 tensor cores.

Two questions:

- Does the `VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT` path cover **V4.1** checkpoints, or only V4? The re-encode itself looks model-agnostic, but I'd like to confirm the scale-mapping assumption holds for the V4.1 expert layout.
- Your measurements are prefill-side on V4-Flash-0731. Our production traffic is **prefill-light / decode-heavy**, so I'm most interested in the decode side — do you expect the FP8 GEMM to help there as well, or is the win prefill-only?

Happy to validate a branch on our fleet (single-node 8×H20, V4.1-Flash) and post serving-side numbers back here.

detail.title: [Model][Quant] DeepSeek-V4: opt-in MXFP4→block-FP8 expert dequant (Hopper prefill speedup)

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MXFP4 -> block-FP8 expert re-encode must fail closed on inexact input.
+
+The DeepSeek-V4 fp4->fp8 dequant path (``VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1``) accepts
+only inputs whose decoded MXFP4 weight values are exactly representable by the
+block-FP8 result.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.fp4_dequant import (
+    _FP4_LUT,
+    DsV4Fp4DequantMoEMethod,
+    cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block,
+)
+
+
+def _dequant_mxfp4(weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    low = (weight & 0x0F).long()
+    high = ((weight >> 4) & 0x0F).long()
+    vals = torch.stack([_FP4_LUT[low], _FP4_LUT[high]], dim=-1).flatten(1)
+    scl = scale.view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu).float().repeat_interleave(32, dim=1)
+    return vals * scl
+
+
+def _dequant_fp8_block(weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    out_dim, in_dim = weight.shape
+    bs = 128
+    w = weight.float().view(out_dim // bs, bs, in_dim // bs, bs).transpose(1, 2)
+    s = scale.float().view(out_dim // bs, in_dim // bs, 1, 1)
+    return (w * s).transpose(1, 2).reshape(out_dim, in_dim)
+
+
+def _make_expert(
+    packed_weight: int = 0x11, scale_byte: int = 127
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    weight = torch.full((128, 64), packed_weight, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    scale = torch.full((128, 4), scale_byte, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    return weight, scale
+
+
+def _assert_exact_conversion(weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    ref = _dequant_mxfp4(weight, scale)
+    fp8_w, block_scale = cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(weight, scale)
+    got = _dequant_fp8_block(fp8_w, block_scale)
+    assert fp8_w.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    assert torch.equal(ref, got)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "out_dim,in_dim", [(256, 256), (256, 512), (512, 256), (128, 1024)]
+)
+def test_cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block_is_lossless(out_dim: int, in_dim: int):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    weight = torch.randint(0, 256, (out_dim, in_dim // 2), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    # e8m0 exponents around a realistic range (bias 127): 2**-8 .. 2**0.
+    scale = torch.randint(127 - 8, 127 + 1, (out_dim, in_dim // 32), dtype=torch.uint8)
+
+    _assert_exact_conversion(weight, scale)
+
+
+def test_cast_rejects_byte_110_underflow():
+    weight, scale = _make_expert()
+    scale[0, 0] = 110
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not exactly representable"):
+        cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(weight, scale)
+
+
+def test_cast_rejects_non_finite_e8m0_scale():
+    weight, scale = _make_expert(packed_weight=0)
+    scale[0, 0] = 255
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="1 invalid E8M0 scale"):
+        cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(weight, scale)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "small_scale,packed_weight,exact",
+    [
+        (113, 0x11, True),  # 0.5 * 2**(6 - 14) is the minimum e4m3 subnormal.
+        (112, 0x11, False),  # The same value at spread 15 is not representable.
+        (110, 0x66, True),  # 4.0 remains representable at spread 17.
+    ],
+)
+def test_cast_checks_exactness_per_value(
+    small_scale: int, packed_weight: int, exact: bool
+):
+    weight, scale = _make_expert(packed_weight=packed_weight)
+    scale[0, 0] = small_scale
+
+    if exact:
+        _assert_exact_conversion(weight, scale)
+    else:
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not exactly representable"):
+            cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(weight, scale)
+
+
+def test_cast_rejects_extreme_scale_spread_without_float32_false_pass():
+    weight, scale = _make_expert()
+    scale[0, 0] = 0
+    scale[0, 1] = 254
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not exactly representable"):
+        cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(weight, scale)
+
+
+def test_process_failure_does_not_replace_layer_parameters():
+    weight, invalid_scale = _make_expert(packed_weight=0)
+    invalid_scale[0, 0] = 255
+    _, valid_scale = _make_expert(packed_weight=0)
+
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.register_parameter(
+        "w13_weight",
+        torch.nn.Parameter(weight.unsqueeze(0), requires_grad=False),
+    )
+    layer.register_parameter(
+        "w13_weight_scale",
+        torch.nn.Parameter(invalid_scale.unsqueeze(0), requires_grad=False),
+    )
+    layer.register_parameter(
+        "w2_weight",
+        torch.nn.Parameter(weight.unsqueeze(0).clone(), requires_grad=False),
+    )
+    layer.register_parameter(
+        "w2_weight_scale",
+        torch.nn.Parameter(valid_scale.unsqueeze(0), requires_grad=False),
+    )
+    original_parameters = dict(layer._parameters)
+    method = object.__new__(DsV4Fp4DequantMoEMethod)
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Validated MXFP4 -> block-FP8 expert dequant for DeepSeek-V4 on Hopper.
+
+DeepSeek-V4 Instruct checkpoints ship MXFP4 (e2m1 + e8m0 microscale) routed
+experts. On Hopper (SM90) the default MXFP4 path runs the Marlin W4A16 kernel.
+When ``VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1`` we instead re-encode exactly representable
+experts to block-FP8 (e4m3, 128x128 scales) at load time and run them through
+the existing block-FP8 MoE kernel, which uses FP8 tensor cores for materially
+higher prefill throughput. Loading fails before replacing layer parameters if
+an invalid e8m0 scale or an inexact weight conversion is found. The trade-off
+is larger expert weight memory (FP8 is 2x MXFP4).
+
+Exactness here applies to decoded MXFP4 weight values accepted by the load-time
+check. The FP8 execution path still uses dynamic activation quantization.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm import envs
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8Config, Fp8MoEMethod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.mxfp4 import Mxfp4MoEMethod
+
+# e2m1 (FP4) code -> value lookup table (sign bit is the high code bit).
+_FP4_LUT = torch.tensor(
+    [
+        0.0,
+        0.5,
+        1.0,
+        1.5,
+        2.0,
+        3.0,
+        4.0,
+        6.0,
+        0.0,
+        -0.5,
+        -1.0,
+        -1.5,
+        -2.0,
+        -3.0,
+        -4.0,
+        -6.0,
+    ],
+    dtype=torch.float32,
+)
+
+# Largest exponent spread for which each e2m1 code remains exactly
+# representable after normalization to an e4m3fn block. Zero is unrestricted.
+_FP4_MAX_EXACT_SCALE_SPREAD = torch.tensor(
+    [255, 14, 15, 14, 16, 15, 17, 16] * 2,
+    dtype=torch.uint8,
+)
+
+_FP8_BLOCK = 128
+_FP4_GROUP = 32
+# max_fp4 (6.0) * 2**MAX_OFFSET_BITS must fit e4m3 (max 448): 6*2**6=384 < 448.
+_MAX_OFFSET_BITS = 6
+_INVALID_E8M0_SCALE = 0xFF
+
+
+def dsv4_fp4_dequant_enabled() -> bool:
+    """Whether the opt-in MXFP4->FP8 expert dequant path is enabled."""
+    return envs.VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT
+
+
+def _raise_for_conversion_issues(issue_counts: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    invalid_scales, inexact_values = issue_counts.detach().cpu().tolist()
+    if invalid_scales or inexact_values:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MXFP4->FP8 conversion rejected: "
+            f"{invalid_scales} invalid E8M0 scale value(s), "
+            f"{inexact_values} weight value(s) not exactly representable "
+            "as block E4M3FN"
+        )
+
+
+def _cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    if weight.ndim != 2 or scale.ndim != 2:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MXFP4->FP8 requires 2D weight and scale tensors, "
+            f"got weight.ndim={weight.ndim} scale.ndim={scale.ndim}"
+        )
+    if weight.dtype != torch.uint8 or scale.dtype != torch.uint8:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MXFP4->FP8 requires uint8 weight and scale tensors, "
+            f"got weight.dtype={weight.dtype} scale.dtype={scale.dtype}"
+        )
+    if weight.device != scale.device:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MXFP4->FP8 requires weight and scale on the same device, "
+            f"got weight.device={weight.device} scale.device={scale.device}"
+        )
+
+    out_dim, in_half = weight.shape
+    in_dim = in_half * 2
+    if in_dim % _FP8_BLOCK or out_dim % _FP8_BLOCK:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"MXFP4->FP8 requires dims divisible by {_FP8_BLOCK}, "
+            f"got out={out_dim} in={in_dim}"
+        )
+    expected_scale_shape = (out_dim, in_dim // _FP4_GROUP)
+    if tuple(scale.shape) != expected_scale_shape:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MXFP4->FP8 scale shape mismatch: "
+            f"expected {expected_scale_shape}, got {tuple(scale.shape)}"
+        )
+
+    invalid_scale = scale == _INVALID_E8M0_SCALE
+    safe_scale = scale.masked_fill(invalid_scale, 127)
+
+    low = weight & 0x0F
+    high = (weight >> 4) & 0x0F
+    codes = torch.stack([low, high], dim=-1).flatten(1)
+    lut = _FP4_LUT.to(weight.device)
+    x = lut[codes.long()]
+
+    b_out, b_in = out_dim // _FP8_BLOCK, in_dim // _FP8_BLOCK
+    code_blocks = codes.view(b_out, _FP8_BLOCK, b_in, _FP8_BLOCK).transpose(1, 2)
+    scale_blocks = safe_scale.view(
+        b_out, _FP8_BLOCK, b_in, _FP8_BLOCK // _FP4_GROUP
+    ).transpose(1, 2)
+    max_scale = scale_blocks.amax(dim=(2, 3), keepdim=True)
+    scale_spread = (max_scale - scale_blocks).repeat_interleave(_FP4_GROUP, dim=-1)
+    max_exact_spread = _FP4_MAX_EXACT_SCALE_SPREAD.to(weight.device)[code_blocks.long()]
+    inexact_value = scale_spread > max_exact_spread
+    issue_counts = torch.stack(
+        [invalid_scale.count_nonzero(), inexact_value.count_nonzero()]
+    )
+
+    scl = safe_scale.view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu).float()
+    scl = scl.view(b_out, _FP8_BLOCK, b_in, -1).transpose(1, 2).flatten(2)
+    block_scale = scl.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True) / (2**_MAX_OFFSET_BITS)
+    offset = scl / block_scale
+    offset = offset.unflatten(-1, (_FP8_BLOCK, -1)).repeat_interleave(
+        _FP4_GROUP, dim=-1
+    )
+    x = x.view(b_out, _FP8_BLOCK, b_in, _FP8_BLOCK).transpose(1, 2)
+    fp8_weight = (x * offset).transpose(1, 2).reshape(out_dim, in_dim)
+    return (
+        fp8_weight.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        block_scale.squeeze(-1).float(),
+        issue_counts,
+    )
+
+
+def cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Re-encode one MXFP4 expert weight to block-FP8 exactly or fail.
+
+    Args:
+        weight: uint8 ``[out, in // 2]`` MXFP4 weights (two e2m1 nibbles/byte).
+        scale: uint8 ``[out, in // 32]`` e8m0 microscale, one per 32-elem group.
+
+    Returns:
+        A tuple ``(fp8_weight, block_scale)`` where ``fp8_weight`` is
+        float8_e4m3fn ``[out, in]`` and ``block_scale`` is float32
+        ``[out // 128, in // 128]``.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If the tensor layout is unsupported, an e8m0 scale is
+            invalid, or any decoded MXFP4 value is not exactly representable.
+
+    """
+    fp8_weight, block_scale, issue_counts = _cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(weight, scale)
+    _raise_for_conversion_issues(issue_counts)
+    return fp8_weight, block_scale
+
+
+def _convert_experts(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    weights, scales, issue_counts = [], [], []
+    for e in range(weight.shape[0]):
+        w, s, issues = _cast_mxfp4_to_fp8_block(weight[e], scale[e])
+        weights.append(w)
+        scales.append(s)
+        issue_counts.append(issues)
+    return (
+        torch.stack(weights),
+        torch.stack(scales),
+        torch.stack(issue_counts).sum(dim=0),
+    )
+
+
+class DsV4Fp4DequantMoEMethod(Fp8MoEMethod):
+    """Load MXFP4 experts, validate exactness, then run the FP8 MoE kernel."""
+
+    supports_pre_processed_weights = False
+
+    def __init__(self, layer):
+        super().__init__(
+            Fp8Config(
+                is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=True,
+                activation_scheme="dynamic",
+                weight_block_size=[_FP8_BLOCK, _FP8_BLOCK],
+            ),
+            layer,
+        )
+        self._mxfp4 = Mxfp4MoEMethod(layer.moe_config)
+
+    def create_weights(
+        self,
+        layer,
+        num_experts,
+        hidden_size,
+        intermediate_size_per_partition,
+        params_dtype,
+        **extra_weight_attrs,
+    ):
+        self._mxfp4.create_weights(
+            layer,
+            num_experts,
+            hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size_per_partition,
+            params_dtype,
+            **extra_weight_attrs,
+        )
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer) -> None:
+        w13, w13_scale, w13_issues = _convert_experts(
+            layer.w13_weight.data, layer.w13_weight_scale.data
+        )
+        w2, w2_scale, w2_issues = _convert_experts(
+            layer.w2_weight.data, layer.w2_weight_scale.data
+        )
+        _raise_for_conversion_issues(w13_issues + w2_issues)
+
+        for name in ("w13_weight_scale", "w2_weight_scale"):
+            layer._parameters.pop(name, None)
+
+        layer.w13_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w13, requires_grad=False)
+        layer.w2_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w2, requires_grad=False)
+        layer.register_parameter(
+            "w13_weight_scale_inv",
+            torch.nn.Parameter(w13_scale, requires_grad=False),
+        )
+        layer.register_parameter(
+            "w2_weight_scale_inv",
+            torch.nn.Parameter(w2_scale, requires_grad=False),
+        )
+        layer.w13_input_scale = None
+        layer.w2_input_scale = None
+        layer.weight_block_size = [_FP8_BLOCK, _FP8_BLOCK]
+        super().process_weights_after_loading(layer)

@@ -224,6 +224,13 @@ def get_quant_method(self, layer, prefix):
                         quant_config=self._get_nvfp4_config(),
                         moe_config=layer.moe_config,
                     )
+                from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.fp4_dequant import (
+                    DsV4Fp4DequantMoEMethod,
+                    dsv4_fp4_dequant_enabled,
+                )
+
+                if dsv4_fp4_dequant_enabled():
+                    return DsV4Fp4DequantMoEMethod(layer)
                 return Mxfp4MoEMethod(layer.moe_config, activation_key=kMxfp8Dynamic)
             # expert_dtype == "fp8": fall through to Fp8Config which
             # returns Fp8MoEMethod with block-wise float32 scales.

Additional throughput A/B on Hopper for this opt-in path (H20, TP=4, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--max-model-len 524288`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, 32 concurrent requests, 0% prefix-cache hit). Throughput read from the engine's Prometheus counters (`vllm:generation_tokens_total` / `vllm:prompt_tokens_total`), reported as total tokens / wall time.

### Decode (1-token input, forced N-token output via `ignore_eos`, 32 concurrent)

| output len | default (Marlin W4A16) | this PR (dequant->FP8) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2k  | 1,642 tok/s | 1,856 tok/s | 1.13x |
| 10k | 1,637 tok/s | 1,841 tok/s | 1.12x |

Per-request ~51 -> ~58 tok/s. Both engines are fully batched (`Running: 32`), and decode rate is independent of output length. So the FP8-tensor-core expert path also helps decode (~1.13x), not just prefill.

### Prefill (unique random prompts, `max_tokens=1`, 32 concurrent)

| input len | default (Marlin W4A16) | this PR (dequant->FP8) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8k  | 6,545 tok/s | 13,335 tok/s | 2.04x |
| 64k | 8,242 tok/s | 11,370 tok/s | 1.38x |

The prefill speedup narrows as context grows (attention increasingly dominates over the MoE GEMM), but stays positive.

### Trade-off (unchanged)

FP8 experts use 2x the weight memory vs MXFP4, which lowers KV capacity: at this config per-GPU available KV cache is 83.9 GiB (Marlin) -> 53.7 GiB (this PR), i.e. GPU KV cache size 5.70M -> 3.65M tokens. Accuracy is unaffected (GSM8K 1319-item parity, 94.47% vs 93.93%, within noise), as noted in the PR body.

### How to use

Opt-in via the `VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1` env var (default off; without it the model runs the usual MXFP4/Marlin path). Example on Hopper:

```bash
VLLM_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 524288 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
```

To go back to the default (MXFP4/Marlin W4A16), just unset the variable. On startup the worker log shows the FP8 path is active: `Using TRITON Fp8 MoE backend` and the MoE running as `fp8_w8a8` block `[128, 128]`.

We have complementary gfx942 / DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash work for this design and would prefer to coordinate it with this PR rather than open another generic MXFP4-to-FP8 loader.

Our local TP8 checkpoint experiment keeps the existing packed-W4 shard loading, then converts only routed experts before native block-FP8 kernel setup. The additional ROCm/V4.1 contracts we found are:

- **Gate/up padding:** the TP-local intermediate width is 288, which is not 128-aligned. Gate and up halves must be padded separately to 384; padding the concatenated tensor changes the gate/up split.
- **FP8 format handling:** FN-to-FNUZ normalization and scale compensation should stay in the existing ROCm FP8 method rather than being implemented as raw E4M3FN byte reinterpretation.
- **Checkpoint metadata:** dense UE8M0 interpretation and the checkpoint-wide `expert_dtype=fp4` remain unchanged. Only routed-expert compute state and the padded extent change.
- **Clamp semantics:** the positive clamp of 10 must survive the selected MoE dispatch. Our separate evidence on #53875 covers the existing fused SiLU/quant path; equality of stored weights alone is not sufficient to establish model-output equivalence.

On the historical local implementation, all 320 layer/rank expert conversions had zero relative RMSE against decoded W4 values. Independent TP8 arithmetic checks and changed-input graph replays passed before model loading. GSM8K-100 completed at 99%, which we treat only as an initial corruption screen, not paired quality qualification. Resident expert memory, including padding and scales, increased by 2.5104167x.

These results are **not tests of this PR's current head**, and we are not claiming a current-main incremental serving gain.

Would an opt-in ROCm/V4.1 extension with platform-native dtype handling and separate gate/up padding fit the intended scope of this PR, or would you prefer it as a follow-up after the base conversion lands? We will keep the code local and human-review it before any submission.

Follow-up from the AMD/TP8 review against `b575b5fc05d65a809c68cf3137ac925b3fb30294`.

### 1. Existing ROCm normalization should be reused

`Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` already performs FN-to-FNUZ normalization and scale compensation. I verified that tensor arithmetic against the re-encoded values on CPU, so an additional byte reinterpretation in this loader would be unnecessary.

### 2. The current MXFP4 conversion is not unconditionally lossless

This limitation is platform-independent.

A 128x128 matrix of packed `0x11` weights, with microscale byte 127 except for one group at byte 110, contains `2^-18` values that the current conversion rounds to zero. Microscale byte 255 also produces non-finite values without rejection.

These are synthetic contract counterexamples, not evidence that a released checkpoint contains either case. The existing exactness test samples scale bytes 119..127, so it does not exercise these boundaries.

I have a local fail-closed reconstruction check plus a 128-aligned allocation extension for 288-wide TP shards. The allocation change uses the packed loader's existing separate gate/up halves and unpadded rank offsets; it does not change global `expert_dtype` or dense UE8M0 scales.

Initial local status:
- 13 CPU source-contract cases pass.
- Both new rejection cases fail against the parent implementation as expected.
- These tests exercise extracted tensor/loader logic only. They do not establish native loading, ROCm execution, clamp correctness, or model quality.

### 3. Native gfx942 loader qualification

A later native pass reached 36 actual-import CPU/GPU tests across all eight TP offsets and the conversion/normalization cases.

That exposed an ordering constraint: `Fp8MoEMethod` chooses/refines its backend before the later dimension-rounding hook. A local width of 288 therefore selects an unsupported 32x32 block scheme unless the method's copied config is 128-aligned before backend selection.

Keeping checkpoint metadata unpadded while changing that internal ordering passes native allocation and FN/FNUZ post-load checks for eight synthetic experts. The observed extra allocation cost was roughly 1.8-2.4 s and 122-123 MiB peak HBM in this synthetic test, not a full-checkpoint measurement.

The loaded expert was not yet qualified at this point: M=1 failed the independent positive-clamp oracle, and the selected two-stage CK SiLU path exposes no stage-1 clamp argument. I did not treat this as evidence about split-K or other arithmetic, and no model startup or serving claim followed.

### 4. Native layer compute qualification

A subsequent guarded Triton fallback passed the native layer compute gate.

Two changes were required:

1. Preserve the requested FP8 backend while giving the temporary MXFP4 allocation helper its own `auto` backend.
2. Exclude clamp-active inputs from the existing unclamped SiLU/block128-FP8 shortcut, matching the guard already discussed in #53875.

With those changes, 40 actual-import CPU/GPU tests pass. Real packed allocation/post-loading and clamped M=1/8/16 forwards pass the unchanged independent FP32 oracle, along with three changed-route graph replays per size. Eager NRMSE was 0.059519 / 0.051727 / 0.055704. M=1 is close to the 0.06 bound, so this is still not a substitute for full checkpoint/model validation.

A four-arm diagnostic also separated two CK issues: the M=1 split-K defect and ignored positive clamp are distinct. Disabling split-K repairs only the unclamped case. We are not claiming a CK fix.

### Scope

All of the above is local candidate work with packaged vLLM / Torch / ROCm dependencies. It is **not** a test of this entire PR head or current main, and there is still no endpoint speedup claim.

The extension remains local pending human review, coordination on the base PR, full-checkpoint coverage, and paired model testing. I will not open a duplicate loader PR while this work is being coordinated here.

Thanks for the careful counterexamples and for keeping the ROCm work coordinated here. I confirmed both issues against `b575b5fc`.

The current unconditional **lossless** wording is too broad:

- With a block maximum scale byte of 127, byte 110 gives `s = 2^-17`. For an E2M1 value of 0.5, the value presented to E4M3FN is `0.5 * 64 * 2^-17 = 2^-12`, below E4M3FN's minimum positive subnormal (`2^-9`). It therefore rounds to zero even though the decoded source value is `2^-18`.
- Scale byte 255 propagates a non-finite value through `amax` and the block scale, and the current conversion does not reject it.

The existing exactness test samples scale bytes only in `119..127`, so it proves exactness for that sampled range, not for arbitrary MXFP4 scales. Likewise, the successful DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 load and model evaluations are useful corruption/non-inferiority checks, but they are not an exhaustive load-time reconstruction check. I therefore cannot claim from the current evidence that every tensor in the released checkpoint satisfies an unconditional exactness contract. Conversely, the synthetic cases do not show that the released checkpoint actually contains such values.

I agree this should fail closed before retaining any lossless claim. The fix I intend for this PR is to:

1. reject invalid/non-finite E8M0 scales before conversion;
2. verify that every normalized source value is exactly representable after the E4M3FN cast before replacing the layer parameters;
3. add targeted tests for the byte-110 underflow and byte-255 cases, plus the exactness boundary; and
4. narrow the wording to **lossless for inputs accepted by the load-time exactness check**.

The validation can be aggregated on device and checked once per converted tensor/layer so that it does not add a host synchronization per expert. Until a full checkpoint scan reports zero mismatches, I will keep the released-checkpoint claim limited to the serving/evaluation evidence already reported.

For scope, I would prefer to land the platform-independent correctness contract and fail-closed checks here first, then handle the ROCm/V4.1 extension as a coordinated follow-up. The separate gate/up padding, FN/FNUZ handling, backend-selection ordering, clamp behavior, and CK/Triton fallback are substantial platform-specific contracts and deserve their own review and validation rather than being folded into this correction. Please keep the local work; it sounds directly useful once this base is solid.

We run **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (not V4) in production on a single node of 8×H20 (SM90) with stock MXFP4/Marlin, so we're a direct candidate for this opt-in path. Two things that may be useful:
